cards.text: Isaiah, the LORD's prophet, has just described priests and prophets who stagger from wine (Isaiah 28:7-8). Now the word of the LORD comes for the scoffers who rule the people in Jerusalem, because they said, "We have made a covenant with death; we have fashioned an agreement with Sheol." Out of EVERYBODY in the world to sign a deal with, they picked DEATH.

cards.question: The rulers in Jerusalem say they've made a deal with death and Sheol. What do they think it gets them?

answers.text: The scourge will not touch them

cards.text: Then they say what their safety rests on, right out loud: "because we have made lies our refuge and falsehood our hiding place." Friend, that's putting tape over the check engine light and calling the car FIXED.
So the Lord GOD answers them. But before He says a word about their hiding place, He talks about a stone He's laying.

cards.question: The Lord GOD is speaking to the rulers in Jerusalem. He says He's laying a stone in ___.

cards.text: He calls it "a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation…" Peter, an apostle of Jesus, quotes this stone line in his first letter and applies it to Jesus (1 Peter 2:4-6).

cards.question: The Lord GOD says the one who believes will never be shaken.

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD says, "I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level." Friend, the shelves in my bakery have NEVER met a level, and every cookie jar on them slowly slides to one end.

cards.question: The Lord GOD says water will flood the rulers' hiding place. What does He say will sweep away their refuge of lies?
The Lord GOD says the rulers' covenant with death will stand.
The rulers were sure the overwhelming scourge would pass them by. The Lord GOD says that when it passes through, they will be ___ by it.
The Lord GOD says the overwhelming scourge will pass through just one time.

cards.text: It will sweep through morning after morning, by day and by night, and carry them away. Understanding this message will bring sheer terror.

Then Isaiah gives a picture from everyday life: "the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to wrap around you." Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer under a pile of old paper, and NOT ONE takeout menu ever covered my whole mustache.

Then Isaiah says the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim, where He broke out against David's enemies, the Philistines (2 Samuel 5:20). He will rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, where He fought for Israel in Joshua's day (Joshua 10:10-14).

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD will rise up to do His work and perform His task. How does Isaiah describe that work and that task?
Isaiah warns the scoffers to stop mocking. If they don't, what does he say will happen to their shackles?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says he has heard from the Lord GOD of Hosts "a decree of destruction against the whole land."
Now Isaiah says, "Listen and hear my voice. Pay attention and hear what I say." And then the prophet does something nobody saw coming: he starts talking about FARMING.

cards.question: Isaiah asks, "Does the plowman plow for planting every day?" What does the farmer actually do with his field?

answers.text: He levels it and then plants
He keeps plowing all year long
He leaves it to rest a year

cards.text: Once the ground is leveled, the farmer sows caraway and scatters cumin. Friend, plowing every day and never planting is me preheating the oven for three weeks and never baking ONE cookie.

cards.question: Isaiah says the farmer throws his wheat, barley and rye all together into one big pile of seed.
Caraway and cumin scattered, wheat in rows, barley in plots, rye within its border. Isaiah says the farmer knows how because his ___ instructs and teaches him properly.

cards.text: Then comes the harvest. Isaiah says caraway is not threshed with a sledge, and a cart wheel is not rolled over the cumin.

cards.question: The farmer doesn't use a threshing sledge on his caraway. What does he beat it out with instead?

cards.text: A stick for the caraway and a rod for the cumin. Different seed, different tool, the same way you don't press a delicate sugar cookie with a sledgehammer, and friend, I have the FLAT cookie to prove it.

cards.question: Isaiah says the farmer does not keep threshing grain for bread forever.

cards.text: The cart wheels may roll over the grain, but the horses do not crush it. And Isaiah says this also comes from the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: Isaiah says all this also comes from the LORD of Hosts. How does he describe the LORD?

answers.text: Wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom
Mighty in battle and fearsome in strength
Gracious in mercy and abounding in love
